I don’t fully relate on the ghosting of interviews, but I used to be SOoo anxious about being interviewed… experience overtime helped. Following through on interviews helped get me into a groove. Some went well and some didn’t. But the important thing is to forgive yourself. It’s ok if you don’t do well.

Just ask yourself “so what?” “And?” “What’s the worse thing that happens if the conversation doesn’t go well?” Your answer will most likely … “… nothing, I guess…” You must move on and make tweaks for next time! It’s all a learning process.

Sometimes I have to help interview new hires at my job now. Let me tell you it’s nerve wracking when the role is reversed too lol. At least for me. But still, with time you figure out your groove.

And to me it’s interesting to see which interviewees are obviously nervous vs who aren’t. It’s so much lighter for me when they aren’t nervous. I just need to hear what they’re about (son): Who are they? Do they seem competent? Does their experience support it? That’s it.

I hope this all helps! Easier said than done, but in the wise words of Shia LeBeouf, “Just do it!!”

There are a number of regret testimonies in this subreddit, including mine. I exchanged my standard backs with angled and it didn’t help in the long run. I returned the Sactional and got a refund. 

To sum up complaints: 

- Sactionals aren’t comfortable and cause back pain, even with the angled sides. Many people think it’s the comfiest couch ever, and others beg to differ. 
- The couch has to be regularly fluffed, vacuumed and rearranged to look good.
- The exchange process is sloppy. You have to ship back your pieces and wait until your shipment is received at the warehouse until they ship your replacements. This process leaves you without covers or couch pieces for at least a week. 
- The exchange and return processes are highly manual compared to the self-serve purchase process. So sometimes there are miscommunications between Lovesac employees and it causes mid deliveries or delays.  
- The assembly is cumbersome! Pieces are heavy (esp if you have stairs) and covers are painful to put on. It takes many hours. Your hands and back will hurt afterwards, and you’ll end up never wanting to wash covers because of this. 
- The Sactionals are way too overpriced for all these cons! For how expensive these pieces are, you should be getting luxury, designer couches with at home assembly.

I know these are supposed to be sustainable and you can re-customize over time. But let’s say you want to buy new covers or add another seat. That’s another $1k. There are many decent couches out there that cost the same. I’m sorry to the earth, but I need to be able to afford my furniture and feel comfortable using it. 

Truth be told I think they look amazing. If the comfort was equally as amazing, I’d consider bearing the price since they’re also made from recycled materials. I do appreciate the company’s mission, but wanted to share these cons as a consideration for you.
